concept: Randomized Hamiltonian simulation variants trade sample cost, precision scaling, and circuit structure
summary: qDRIFT provides a simple randomized product formula, while related methods such as stochastic Hamiltonian sparsification and qSWIFT modify the randomized compilation strategy to improve performance in intermediate gate-budget or high-precision regimes.
limitations: qSWIFT introduces additional structure, including an ancilla-based construction in the cited source.
Stochastic sparsification changes the simulated Hamiltonian distribution and requires probability choices for retained terms.
These variants are not yet implemented as OpenQEvo methods.
implications: Treat qDRIFT as the currently executable randomized baseline.
Use qSWIFT and sparsification sources to guide future randomized-method metadata and implementation decisions.
Do not recommend qSWIFT or sparsification as executable until registered methods exist.

evidence.note: Describes qSWIFT as a higher-order randomized compiler with improved precision scaling relative to qDRIFT.
Describes stochastic Hamiltonian sparsification as interpolating between qDRIFT and randomized first-order Trotterization.
